extraction.name: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
extraction.description: The paper presents a systematic study on object hallucination of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) and proposes a polling-based query method called POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) for better evaluation of object hallucination.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.publisher: Renmin University of China, Meituan Group
extraction.rai:dataCollection: POPE constructs evaluation triples consisting of an image, multiple questions, and their answers ('Yes' or 'No'). Ground-truth objects are extracted from human annotations or automatic segmentation tools. Nonexistent objects are sampled using Random, Popular, or Adversarial settings.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with 'Yes' answers are built using ground-truth objects. Questions with 'No' answers are built by sampling negative objects using three strategies: Random Sampling, Popular Sampling (top-k most frequent objects in the dataset not in the image), and Adversarial Sampling (top-k frequent co-occurring objects not in the image).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Randomly selected 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations from the validation set of MSCOCO, and constructed 6 questions for each image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Objects in the image are obtained either from existing human annotations or automatic segmentation tools. The ratio between ground-truth and nonexistent objects is set to 1:1 for label balance. Questions are formulated using the template 'Is there a/an <object> in the image?'
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEEM (Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once), ChatGPT
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The hallucination phenomenon hinders the safe use of LVLMs in real-world deployment, as it may result in unexpected consequences. For example, an autonomous driving system could make wrong decisions due to incorrect understanding of the external environment, leading to serious safety issues.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LVLMs are prone to hallucinate objects that frequently appear in the visual instruction datasets or frequently co-occur with ground-truth objects in the image.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation only focuses on object hallucination and does not measure overall LVLM capacity. Evaluations were conducted on a subset of validation sets due to compute limits. The matching-based method may fail if LVLMs do not explicitly output 'Yes' or 'No'. Automatic segmentation tools may produce labels inconsistent with human annotations. Only a small number of LVLMs were evaluated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and Validation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) for object hallucination.
